//: Art-direction retunes applied on top of a derived library item. Each entry names the defect it fixes (from the 2026-11-09 output/gen review) and the exact operation. Maps are re-derived from the retuned albedo so normal/roughness stay consistent. No model retraining.

iron_directorate__metal_trim.because: review: glossy blue padded blocks; wrong surface language for polished gunmetal

gunmetal_worn.because: review: flat and low-contrast; needs value separation

iron_directorate__armour_secondary.because: review: gold chevron reads as an insignia, motif too large for a 256 tile. Measured at the pixel tier this is not a sheet fault: at a 0.35 m texture tile and a 2 cm texel grid the gold band is ~2 texels, so it reads as trim. The source tile size is left physically correct and the texel grid performs the abstraction.

deck_plate_industrial.because: review: the floor tile reads as a plain slab. The generated sheet carries a warm oil/rust cast across most of its area, which at a 2 cm texel grid and a 64-colour palette locks to leather-brown instead of industrial steel. Neutralise the alloy and keep the wear as value, not hue. Second fault found at 256 px: one 2 m texture tile put the diamond tread at ~3.5 texels, which locks to noise. The world size of one tile is doubled, so the tread reads at ~7 texels and the geometric panel seam carries the deck module.

gunmetal_polished.because: measured on the pixel master: median render luma 138/255, i.e. light grey plastic, not IoA steel. The generated sheet is a bright showroom alloy; stretch its values down so a lit facet lands on the 74-104 palette steps.
